- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 2–5% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day window; if forecast deviates >3% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.8+) followed by model overforecasting — often leads to “overshoot” in next 3–5 days; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is low but price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slightly (1–2%) to reflect hidden bullish sentiment.
